insights.headline: Gold drifts toward $4,150 as a firmer dollar offsets Middle East escalation; MCX gold holds near Rs 1.48 lakh.
insights.summary: Spot gold traded in a tight $4,150-$4,195 band on Friday as a modest dollar rebound and 89% odds of a December Fed hike capped safe-haven gains, even as Houthi missiles struck Aden's presidential palace and US strike plans on Iran were reported. On MCX, December gold rose 0.6% to Rs 148,320 per 10 grams and silver 1.4% to Rs 213,570 a kg on the weak dollar. In India, physical demand cooled as prices rebounded — discounts narrowed to $6 an ounce from $14. RBI's rupee defence has cost $60 billion in six weeks.
points: Middle East war escalates: Houthi missiles hit Aden palace, France sends assets to Saudi Arabia — but the dollar, not gold, is getting the safe-haven bid.
September US CPI 3.7% and PPI 6.3% keep a December Fed hike 89% priced; 10-year yield near 5.11%.
MCX Dec gold +0.6% at Rs 148,320/10g; Dec silver +1.4% at Rs 213,570/kg; COMEX gold $4,195.3, silver $57.99.
India physical demand sluggish as domestic gold rebounded to ~Rs 150,900/10g; discounts narrowed to $6/oz from $14.
RBI has spent $60 billion defending the rupee in six weeks; Brent crude eased near $105 after touching $110.

trending.title: Escalation versus tightening: two safe havens, one winner
trending.summary: The Middle East war is widening — Aden, Riyadh's airport, Iranian targets — yet gold is slipping toward $4,150 because a resurgent dollar and 89% December Fed-hike odds are the stronger pull.

trending.title: Inflation keeps December hike alive — but October is off the table
trending.summary: September CPI (3.7%) and PPI (6.3%) were both hot, yet Fed Chair Kevin Warsh refused to signal an October move, cutting those odds to about 15%. Markets now eye the Oct 27-28 meeting.

trending.title: India's festive buyer waits for the dip
trending.summary: Domestic gold rebounded from a two-month low to ~Rs 150,900/10g and demand stalled; discounts shrank to $6/oz from $14. Dealers say a premium needs festive investment demand like last year's.

trending.title: Rupee defence bill keeps rising
trending.summary: RBI has sold $60 billion in six weeks to defend the rupee; the currency's weakness continues to inflate domestic bullion costs for Indian buyers even when global prices soften.

items.title: Gold slips near $4,150 as dollar rebounds and Middle East war escalates
items.summary: Gold slipped toward $4,150 an ounce in Asian trading as a modest dollar rebound and firmer US Treasury yields capped gains. The pullback came despite a sharp Middle East escalation: Houthi missiles struck Aden's presidential palace, France began deploying military assets to Saudi Arabia, and the US prepared strike plans against Iranian sites.

items.title: Gold holds near $4,170 as inflation keeps December Fed tightening in play
items.summary: Spot gold steadied near $4,172 an ounce while spot silver traded near $57.63 in early US trading on Friday after hot inflation prints — September CPI at 3.7% and PPI at 6.3% annually. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal an October hike, cutting those odds to about 15%, but markets still price an 89% chance of a December increase. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to near 5.11%.

items.title: India Bullion: Up on weak dollar; market assesses Fed rate outlook
items.summary: MCX December gold rose 0.6% to Rs 148,320 per 10 grams on Friday as the dollar index fell to a two-week low of 101.57, while MCX December silver gained 1.4% to Rs 213,570 a kg. COMEX gold rose 0.6% to $4,195.3 an ounce and COMEX silver 1.5% to $57.99. Fading odds of an October Fed hike and falling US yields supported bullion despite hot US inflation data.

items.title: Gold demand drops in India as prices rebound
items.summary: Indian gold demand turned sluggish this week as domestic prices rebounded to around Rs 150,900 per 10 grams on Friday after hitting a two-month low of Rs 145,538 last week. Dealers quoted discounts of up to $6 an ounce over official prices, down from $14 last week. A Mumbai-based dealer said the market could swing to a premium if festive investment demand picks up as it did last year.

items.title: $60 billion in 6 weeks: RBI's rupee defence comes at a cost
items.summary: India's forex reserves fell roughly $60 billion in six weeks to $726.03 billion on October 9, down from a record $785.71 billion on September 4, as the RBI sold dollars to prop up the rupee. The latest week saw an $8.58 billion drop; foreign investors pulled a net $26.8 billion from local markets this year. Gold reserves slipped $1.32 billion to $105.09 billion.

items.title: Government Cuts Duty Drawback Rates on Gold and Silver Jewellery Exports
items.summary: The finance ministry cut duty drawback rates on gold and silver jewellery exports under Notification 85/2026-Customs (N.T.) dated October 15. Gold jewellery drawback falls 3.1% to ₹1,794.11/g from ₹1,851.99; silver jewellery and articles drop ~9% to ₹26,859.02/kg from ₹29,501.09. The move partly reverses July's incentive hike and trims refunds on imported inputs, squeezing exporter margins.

items.title: Brent crude hits $110 a barrel for first time since May as supply concerns mount
items.summary: Brent crude rose 3.7% to $110 a barrel, its first print there since May, as Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Russia-Ukraine energy attacks kept supply risks high. With crude up over 75% this year, traders are repricing inflation risk into bullion; the US offered 17 million barrels from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

items.title: Gold FoFs halt fresh investments before Diwali: What investors can do
items.summary: About 17 fund houses including Mirae Asset, DSP and Tata have paused fresh lump-sum investments, switch-ins and new SIP/STP registrations into gold ETF funds-of-funds from 15-16 October on SEBI's direction, while existing SIPs, redemptions and direct ETF buying continue. September gold ETF inflows were Rs 4,451 crore.

items.title: RBI sets premature redemption price for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at ₹14,614
items.summary: The RBI fixed the premature redemption price for SGB 2020-21 Series VII at ₹14,614 per unit, due 19 October 2026 (20 Oct is a holiday). The price averages IBJA's 999-purity gold closes for Oct 14–16. Issued at ₹5,051 in Oct 2020, exiting now locks in ~189% gains over six years plus 2.5% annual interest.
points: Redemption price ₹14,614 per unit; due 19 Oct 2026 (20 Oct is a holiday).
Based on the simple average of IBJA 999 gold closing prices for Oct 14, 15 and 16.
Issued at ₹5,051 in Oct 2020 — exit implies ~189% capital gains over six years, plus 2.5% annual interest.
Premature redemption is allowed only on interest payment dates after five years from issue.

items.title: Gold, silver diverge as Fed-pause hopes collide with surging crude
items.summary: Spot gold held near $4,167.90 an ounce (-0.05%) while spot silver fell 0.78% to $56.85 in late Friday US trade. Brent settled at $109.86 and WTI topped $100, and rebounding yields offset a weaker dollar and safe-haven demand. US import prices rose 1.1% m/m and 8.1% y/y. After Chair Warsh gave no October signal, futures priced an 83% chance of no change on Oct 27-28.
points: Spot gold near $4,167.90 (-0.05%); spot silver near $56.85 (-0.78%) in late Friday US trade.
Brent settled at $109.86/bbl and WTI topped $100 as Gulf vessel attacks and Iran tensions intensified.
US import prices +1.1% m/m, +8.1% y/y — the largest annual rise since July 2022.
Futures price ~83% odds of no Fed change on Oct 27-28 after Warsh gave no hike signal; December hike bets persist.
10-year Treasury yield recovered toward 5.12%; the dollar index stayed under pressure.

items.title: Why silver is falling faster than gold: What it means for the next surge
items.summary: CPM Group's Jeffrey Christian notes gold consolidating in a $4,050-$4,200 range while silver has broken below $60 to trade near $55.77, arguing silver's larger industrial-demand share and substitution pressure at high prices explain its steeper fall. He flags the risk of a sharper selloff being followed by strong investment demand and a decisive break above $4,200 for gold.

items.title: Gold (XAU/USD) Price Forecast: Bulls Face Crucial $4,226 Resistance
items.summary: FXEmpire's weekly technical read: gold formed a higher weekly high and higher low, hinting at an attempted reversal of the bearish correction. A decisive move above $4,226 would confirm a bullish daily reversal; until then, holding support above $4,066 stays central. A breakout would project an ABCD measured move toward $4,821.
points: Weekly higher high and higher low hint at a reversal attempt; no close yet above last week's $4,208 high (FXEmpire).
A decisive break above $4,226 confirms a bullish reversal; a rise above this week's $4,217 high signals renewed strength (FXEmpire).
Holding support above $4,066 is central; an ABCD pattern projects a measured move toward $4,821 on a breakout (FXEmpire).

items.title: Gold vs silver vs platinum: Which metal saw biggest rally since last Dussehra? Experts explain outlook
items.summary: Silver is the standout since last Dussehra, up about 47% in rupee terms versus gold's ~26% and platinum's ~10.5%; the rupee's slide and the May duty rise to 15% lifted domestic returns. Silver swung wildly, up 155% by January and now 53% off its peak, so buyers near the top stay at a loss. Mint cites experts who see gold backed by central-bank buying, silver with higher upside but more volatility.
